title: Healthy day evaluation sheet
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y7 lesson 8 (Healthy day evaluation sheet (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 8: Diet, exercise and healthy choices. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: A balanced diet
points: Fruit and vegetables: at least 5 a day

panels.title: Activity
points: About 60 minutes a day on average

model.title: Day: cereal, crisps and fizzy drink, pasta; 20 minutes walking; 7 hours on screens.

Gaps: little fruit and veg, sugary drink, low activity
Change 1: swap fizzy drink for water

questions.q: Give one swap to cut sugar.
questions.a: Water instead of fizzy drink; fruit instead of sweets.

questions.q: Why is a long time sedentary harmful?
questions.a: Less fitness, weaker muscles and bones, poorer mood.

questions.q: Core: Evaluate your own typical day against the guidelines and plan two realistic changes (pupil PDF).
questions.a: Honest evaluation and two specific changes.

questions.q: Extend: In the portal response box, explain one long-term benefit of each change. Start: 'Over time...'
questions.a: For example: Over time, less sugar protects teeth and reduces the risk of type 2 diabetes.

questions.q: Stretch: Explain how fasting in Ramadan can be done healthily (suhur, water, balanced iftar).
questions.a: Eat a slow-release suhur, drink water between iftar and suhur, avoid overeating at iftar.

questions.q: How much activity should young people average a day?
questions.a: B) 60 minutes. The UK guideline is at least 60 minutes a day on average.

questions.q: Moderation means... A) never eating treats B) not too much, not too little C) only eating fruit
questions.a: B) not too much, not too little
options: Not too much, not too little

questions.q: Big question: how do you choose what is better for later?
questions.a: Think of long-term health, use small realistic changes, and remember our body is an amanah.
